questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A spanish-speaking place within the EU, to practice my language abilities without travleling too far away.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only bad thing about the exchange is the ridiculous amount of paperwork. Like this. I'm so tired.

questions.answer: Not much, but I prefer it. Way too many introductions this, introductions that, constantly. We are drowning in practical information from the EU.

questions.answer: My only advice is get a contract and get a recommendation/confirmation from a roommate/resident of the place.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: I really don't remember what registrations we're from KU and which were from Pompeu Fabra. It's all a big fever dreamish blur of endless streams of information at this point.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are not prepared for a shitton of paperwork, don't do it. Otherwise it was fun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The amount of "homework" is bigger but the academic level is lower. Kind of like being back in gymnasium.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More hours, more tasks to hand in but at the same time much more help from the teachers and less independence as a student.
